cards.text: The Israelites are still on the move through the wilderness with Moses, Israel's leader, going camp to camp. They set out and camp at Oboth, then at Iye-abarim in the wilderness opposite Moab, then in the Valley of Zered. Friend, I spent years in a junk drawer without moving an inch, and these folks move three times in three verses.

cards.question: Next they camp across the Arnon, in the wilderness that runs into Amorite territory. Numbers says the Arnon is the border between the Moabites and the ___.
Numbers quotes an old book, the Book of the Wars of the LORD, about the wadis of the Arnon. Those wadis lie along which border?

cards.text: Next stop is Beer, the well, and that's where the LORD speaks to Moses. Friend, a well in the WILDERNESS is like finding a warm cookie at the bottom of a junk drawer.

cards.question: At Beer, the LORD tells Moses to gather the people so He can give them ___.
True or false: at the well, Israel sings a song.

cards.text: The song starts, "Spring up, O well, all of you sing to it!" Then it says the well got hollowed out "with their scepters and with their staffs," and friend, scepters do NOT usually come out for yard work.

cards.question: A scepter isn't exactly a farmer's tool. In Israel's song at the well, who dug it?

cards.text: From the wilderness they keep going: Mattanah, Nahaliel, Bamoth, and on to the valley in Moab where the top of Pisgah overlooks the wasteland. If you're keeping a list, friend, put the pencil down and just know they're still moving.
Then Israel sends messengers to Sihon, king of the Amorites. No sneaking around here, friend: they knock on the front door first.

cards.question: What do Israel's messengers ask Sihon for?

answers.text: Permission to pass through his land
A share of the water in his wells
Soldiers to help them fight Moab

cards.question: True or false: Israel promises Sihon they'll stay on the King's Highway and won't even drink water from any well.
That's about as polite as a request gets. How does Sihon answer Israel?

answers.text: He gathers his whole army and attacks
He lets them pass for a fee
He sends them on a longer road

cards.text: Sihon fights Israel at Jahaz, and Israel puts him to the sword and takes his land, from the Arnon to the Jabbok. Friend, they asked to walk down his hallway, and he lost the WHOLE HOUSE.

cards.question: Israel's new land stops at the border of the Ammonites. Why does the text say it stops there?

cards.text: Israel captures all the cities of the Amorites and moves right in, Heshbon and all its villages included.

cards.question: Heshbon was Sihon's city. Before Israel came, Sihon had fought the former king of ___ and taken all his land as far as the Arnon.

cards.text: That's why the poets say, "Come to Heshbon, let it be rebuilt; let the city of Sihon be restored." Then the poem turns toward Moab.

cards.question: In the poets' lines, what goes out from Heshbon, the city of Sihon?

cards.text: That fire consumed Ar of Moab, and the poets cry, "Woe to you, O Moab!"
Then the poem turns: "But we have overthrown them." The fire came out of Sihon's city and swept over Moab, and now Heshbon itself is destroyed as far as Dibon.
So Israel settles into the land of the Amorites. Then Moses sends spies to a place called Jazer.

cards.question: True or false: after the spies go to Jazer, Israel makes peace with the Amorites living there.

cards.text: Then Israel turns up the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, comes out with his whole army to meet them in battle at Edrei. One king down, and the next one's already lining up.

cards.question: Og and his whole army are out there at Edrei. What's the first thing the LORD tells Moses about Og?
The LORD says He has delivered Og into Moses' hand, and tells Moses to do to Og what he did to ___.
True or false: at Edrei, Og's army survives the battle and escapes back into Bashan.

cards.text: Israel strikes down Og, his sons and his whole army, until no remnant is left, and they take possession of his land. Just as the LORD told Moses, Og was delivered into their hand.
